interface.longDescription:
Inspect and control EasyEDA Pro through version-pinned typed API adapters, managed evidence and seven engineering skills for control, schematics, PCB layout, component libraries, manufacturing release, design review and extension development. The exact legacy read tuple is connected-read-admitted and future mismatches fail closed. Legacy general writers remain runtime-disabled.

Four declaration snapshots inventory 855 distinct methods with schemas, route classifications and concrete omission reasons. API discovery and private implementation do not imply validated execution support. On the current 3.2.209 profile, scoped tools provide environment/editor observations, calculations, managed netlist membership comparison, offline project and library-source readers, public catalog queries, disposable opening and bounded PCB observations. Separate disposable spatial purposes offer Via-only, Line/Via and Arc/Line/Via point/region identity batches, standalone circular SMT Pad points and a distinct generated Component point birth with retained footprint/cache/attribute custody. They require original application-function qualification, explicit bounded math scratch acceptance and trusted renderer-intrinsic assumptions; source implementation is separate from positive connected acceptance. It does not run the selecting public region handler or promise full SDK primitive objects. Separate native visual workflows provide guarded navigation, readiness, fixed resize and original-window or renderer capture. Observations do not prove complete board geometry, connectivity, physical stackup or fabrication readiness. A separately pinned ordinary schematic-page reader observes raw components, pins, attributes and existing contact-cache memberships without compiling a netlist or claiming complete topology. Generated disposable fixture import has its own original ordinary launch, held destination and tracked Promise; SDK settlement remains partial evidence until closed-file and registration acceptance. Catalog requests require network confirmation.

Scoped symbol metadata and document-title workflows retain their own version, ownership and saved-result gates. General schematic, PCB and library writing, explicit Save, unrestricted JavaScript and arbitrary commands remain unavailable on the current profile. Opening can migrate, restore tabs, replay caches and automatically persist files or shared settings. Native acknowledgments, previews and unsaved readback do not establish durability.

A separate disposable footprint source-validation workflow starts its own v2 native owner after checkpoint and complete SQL preflight, captures and seals original source inputs once, and retains cleanup through lost publication acknowledgments. It enables no clocks, create, copy/delete or Save. Its result authority flags remain false. Private native graph, main-response and mixed-clock components remain subject to current eligibility, paired-clock, complete-budget, saved-lifecycle and inverse prerequisites; they are not a complete writer.

The persistent foreground manager replaces verified controllers while Codex stays running. It supports original-client inspection, confirmed abort and release settlement while retaining the original process, Job and helper through uncertainty. Finish helper closure and record settlement, cooperatively retire the original facade and observe its exit before replacement. Never replay consumed actions or reconstruct ownership from historical JSON. Source checks, synthetic tests, native compilation, installation, connected effects and saved/reopened results are separate evidence stages. Consult the capability matrix and task references for exact arguments, supported effects and validation limits.
